title: Flatness lifts through a target nonzerodivisor in a Noetherian local ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $(C,\mathfrak m)$ a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning that $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal. Let $A\to C$ be a ring homomorphism and let $t\in\mathfrak m$ be a nonzerodivisor on $C$, meaning that $tc=0$ implies $c=0$ for all $c\in C$. If $C/tC$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], regarded as an $A$-module through $A\to C\to C/tC$, is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $C$ is flat as an $A$-module. No Noetherian, local, finite-presentation or flatness hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or on $A\to C$ beforehand.

source.place: Tag 062U (lemma-flat-at-x), algebraic kernel-and-Nakayama argument in the proof; the same argument works for arbitrary commutative A, since only C is used as a Noetherian local ring. Used by Tag 063T (lemma-quasi-regular-immersion-flat-at-x).

proof.text: Fix a finitely generated ideal $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\subseteq A$. Put $P=I\otimes_A C$, with its $C$-module structure on the second factor, and let $\mu:P\to C$ send $a\otimes c$ to $\varphi(a)c$, where $\varphi:A\to C$ is the given map. This is $C$-linear, so $K=\ker\mu$ is a $C$-submodule. The elements $a_i\otimes1$ generate $P$: write $a=\sum_i b_i a_i$ to obtain $a\otimes c=\sum_i a_i\otimes\varphi(b_i)c$. Thus $P$ is finite over $C$, and $K$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], using Noetherianity of $C$ only.

source.place: Tag 062U (lemma-flat-at-x), kernel-and-Nakayama argument; supporting Algebra Tags 00HD, 00DF, 00IK and 00DV.

proof.text: Write $D=C/tC$ and $\pi:C\to D$ for the quotient. Tensor the exact sequence $C\xrightarrow{t}C\xrightarrow{\pi}D\to0$ of $A$-modules with $I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], the induced map $q=1\otimes\pi:P\to I\otimes_A D$ has kernel $tP$ and is surjective. The multiplication map $\bar\mu:I\otimes_A D\to D$, $a\otimes\bar c\mapsto\overline{\varphi(a)c}$, is injective: it is the tensor of the injection $I\hookrightarrow A$ with the flat $A$-module $D$, under $A\otimes_A D=D$, by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. On pure tensors $\bar\mu q=\pi\mu$, hence the equality holds on all of $P$.

source.place: Tag 062U (lemma-flat-at-x), kernel-and-Nakayama argument; supporting Algebra Tags 00HD, 00DF, 00IK and 00DV.

proof.text: For $k\in K$, the equality $\bar\mu(q(k))=\pi(\mu(k))=0$ and injectivity of $\bar\mu$ give $q(k)=0$. Hence $k=ty$ for some $y\in P$. Then $0=\mu(k)=t\mu(y)$; since $t$ is a nonzerodivisor on $C$, $\mu(y)=0$, so $y\in K$. Consequently $K\subseteq tK$; the reverse inclusion follows from $C$-linearity of $\mu$. Thus $K=tK$. This diagram chase uses only exactness at the middle term from Step 2; injectivity of multiplication by $t$ on $P$ is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 062U (lemma-flat-at-x), kernel-and-Nakayama argument; supporting Algebra Tags 00HD, 00DF, 00IK and 00DV.

proof.text: The ideal $(t)$ is contained in $\mathfrak m$, and $\mathfrak m$ is the Jacobson radical of $C$ because it is the unique maximal ideal. Step 1 gives finiteness of $K$ over $C$, while Step 3 gives $(t)K=K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] over $C$ to conclude $K=0$. Thus $I\otimes_A C\to C$ is injective for every finitely generated ideal $I\subseteq A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fg-ideal-criterion], $C$ is flat over $A$. Neither this criterion nor Steps 1--3 require $A$ to be Noetherian or local, or the homomorphism to have any finiteness property.
